title: Hazel and the Vow
premise: Coral Halloran, a wedding planner who abandoned her own marriage at the altar ten years ago, has built a career orchestrating other people's happily-ever-afters while answering anonymous letters from 'Hazel,' a prison pen-pal she's never met. When Hazel — real name June Okafor, released after serving time for a crime Coral's testimony helped convict her for — moves in next door, Coral discovers the letters were never charity: they were surveillance of the woman who ruined her life. As the town's harvest festival forces them together, Coral must untangle what really happened the night of the fire, confront her own perjured memory, and choose between the justice that protected her and the truth that could free them both. The story ends at the festival's closing night, where Coral publicly recants her false testimony, June chooses forgiveness over vengeance, and Coral forgives the woman in the mirror enough to say yes to a second chance.
about_author: Dominic Pemberton is the pen name of a former small-town court reporter who spent a decade transcribing other people's worst days before turning to fiction. He writes romance about people who have to earn their endings, and lives in a coastal village where he still attends every harvest festival.

chapters.title: The Vow She Didn't Take
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. While staging a flawless wedding at the harborside inn, Coral freezes at the sight of an unlit candle and flashes back to a fire ten years ago. She covers it professionally, but the bride notices her shaking hands. Emotional beat: competence as armor, and the first crack in it.

chapters.title: Letters to Hazel
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. At home, Coral rereads a shoebox of letters she's written monthly to 'Hazel,' an inmate whose name she found in a case file. The letters are tender but evasive — she never signs her full name or explains why she writes. Beat: guilt dressed up as kindness.

chapters.title: The New Neighbor
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. A moving van arrives next door; the woman unloading boxes is unmistakably the face from Coral's nightmares — older, harder, but June Okafor herself. June greets her warmly, calling her by a name only 'Hazel' should know. Beat: the trap springs shut.

chapters.title: What the Letters Were For
chapters.summary: June's POV. June unpacks ten years of Coral's letters, annotated in red ink — dates cross-checked, lies flagged. Her parole condition was simple: stay near Coral Halloran. We learn June believes Coral lied on the witness stand, and moved here to prove it. Beat: sympathy flips to suspicion.

chapters.title: Festival Season
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. The town council hires Coral to coordinate the harvest festival — the same event where the fire started a decade ago. June volunteers to help, forcing proximity. Their first working day crackles with mutual recognition neither will admit. Beat: forced intimacy, masked hostility.

chapters.title: Cider and Cross-Examination
chapters.summary: June's POV. Over festival planning, June asks careful questions about the night of the fire; Coral answers with rehearsed precision that sounds like truth. June notices Coral flinches at one detail — the position of a locked door. Beat: the first thread pulled loose.

chapters.title: The Groom Who Waited
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Daniel Reyes — the man Coral left at the altar — returns to town as the festival's new fire marshal. His presence reopens the wound: he was the one who pulled her from the burning building, and the one whose testimony sealed June's conviction. Beat: old love, old debt.

chapters.title: A Wedding She Can't Plan
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. A client asks Coral to plan a vow renewal at the exact site of the old fire. She takes the job against every instinct, then has a panic attack in the empty hall. June finds her and, unexpectedly, talks her through it. Beat: enemy as unexpected comfort.

chapters.title: Red Ink
chapters.summary: June's POV. June's sister arrives demanding she abandon the obsession and come home. June reveals the letter that started everything: an anonymous note received in prison claiming Coral saw someone else set the fire. Beat: motive deepens; the mystery gains a third player.

chapters.title: The Locked Door
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Coral revisits her own memory and finds it wrong: the back door was locked when she fled, meaning someone inside locked it after the fire started — and she told police it was open. She begins to doubt which version she testified to, and why. Beat: identity crisis begins.

chapters.title: Two Truths at a Table
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Daniel hosts a dinner for festival staff; Coral and June circle each other while Daniel recounts the rescue with heroic detail that contradicts both women's memories. Alone afterward, June accuses Coral of lying; Coral walks out. Beat: open war declared.

chapters.title: What Survival Cost
chapters.summary: June's POV. Flashback chapter: the fire, June's arrest, her mother's death in the aftermath, and the decade of letters that kept her sane and sharpened her rage. We see why justice outside the law became her only religion. Beat: the antagonist becomes fully human.

chapters.title: The Anonymous Note
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Coral tracks the anonymous note's origin to the courthouse copy shop and finds a receipt signed by the retired detective who worked the case. Someone fed June's hope deliberately. Beat: conspiracy surfaces; stakes rise beyond the two women.

chapters.title: Confession in the Greenhouse
chapters.summary: June's POV. June corners Coral among the festival's flowers and demands the truth. Coral admits she isn't sure what she saw — trauma blurred it, and pressure from Daniel and the detective filled the gaps. June, shaken, realizes vengeance aimed at the wrong target may be all she has left. Beat: raw honesty, fragile truce.

chapters.title: The Vow Renewal
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. The vow renewal ceremony goes beautifully until Coral watches the couple repeat vows she once abandoned, and she breaks down mid-event in front of the whole town. June quietly finishes the coordination, saving the wedding. Beat: public unraveling, private grace.

chapters.title: Daniel's Version
chapters.summary: June's POV. June confronts Daniel with timeline discrepancies; his composure cracks just enough to reveal he arrived at the fire before his official call time — and that the detective coached both witnesses. Beat: the hero of the story revealed as its architect.

chapters.title: Burned Evidence
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Coral finds the detective's old case box in the festival storage attic — including the original door lock report, suppressed at trial. Someone has been keeping it close for ten years. Before she can photograph it, the box disappears. Beat: rising dread; the past fights back.

chapters.title: The Night Before the Festival
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. On the eve of the festival, Coral and June lay out everything they know across June's kitchen table and finally read each other's letters aloud — Coral's guilt, June's annotations, the years of watching each other through paper. They agree to expose the truth together. Beat: enemies become allies; tenderness breaks through.

chapters.title: Closing Night
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. At the festival's closing ceremony, Coral takes the stage and publicly recants her testimony, naming the detective and Daniel's coaching. The crowd erupts; Daniel tries to silence her; June stands beside her and confirms every word. Beat: climax — justice spoken outside any courtroom.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: June's POV. The detective is investigated; Daniel leaves town without apology. June faces the question she's avoided: if revenge is gone, what remains? She reads Coral's very first letter again and finds, beneath the guilt, something like love. Beat: grief giving way to choice.

chapters.title: The Woman in the Mirror
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Coral visits the burned building's ruins one last time and finally forgives the frightened girl who lied to survive. She writes a new letter to Hazel — this one signed, honest, and asking forgiveness outright. Beat: the internal vow fulfilled.

chapters.title: Hazel and the Vow
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. One year later, at the rebuilt hall, June and Coral stand before a small gathering — not a wedding, but a vow exchange of their own making: to tell each other the truth first, always. Coral no longer plans weddings she doesn't believe in; she believes in this one. Beat: resolution — second chances, earned.
